title: Beyond molecular structure: critically assessing machine learning for designing organic photovoltaic materials and devices

metadata.authors: Seifrid M, Lo S, Choi DG, Tom G, Le ML, Li K, Sankar R, Vuong HT, Wakidi H, Yi A, Zhu Z, Schopp N, Peng A, Luginbuhl BR, Nguyen TQ, Aspuru-Guzik A

source_summary: This study evaluates machine learning methods for predicting and designing organic photovoltaic devices, introduces the first comprehensive OPV fabrication dataset, identifies key challenges related to data quality and reporting, and advocates for standardized data practices to enhance ML-driven progress in the field.
abstract: Our study explores the current state of machine learning (ML) as applied to predicting and designing organic photovoltaic (OPV) devices. We outline key considerations for selecting the method of encoding a molecular structure and selecting the algorithm while also emphasizing important aspects of training and rigorously evaluating ML models. This work presents the first comprehensive dataset of OPV device fabrication data mined from the literature. The top models achieve state-of-the-art predictive performance. In particular, we identify an algorithm that is used less frequently, but may be particularly well suited to similar datasets. However, predictive performance remains modest (R2 ≅ 0.6) overall. An in-depth analysis of the dataset attributes this limitation to challenges relating to the size of the dataset, as well as data quality and sparsity. These aspects are directly tied to difficulties imposed by current reporting and publication practices. Advocating for standardized reporting of OPV device fabrication data reporting in publications emerges as crucial to streamline literature mining and foster ML adoption. This comprehensive investigation emphasizes the critical role of both data quantity and quality, and highlights the need for collective efforts to unlock ML's potential to drive advancements in OPV.

methods.value: Curating a comprehensive dataset of OPV device fabrication data and evaluating various structural representations and ML algorithms.

problems.value: The challenge of accurately predicting the power conversion efficiency (PCE) of organic photovoltaic (OPV) devices using machine learning (ML) models.

hypotheses.value: The encoding method of molecular structures and the choice of ML algorithm significantly affect the predictive performance for PCE of OPV devices.

evidence.value: The histogram gradient boosting (HGB) model using Mordred descriptors for molecular structure achieved the best predictive performance with an R2 score of 0.61.

conclusions.value: Data quality and standardized reporting are critical for improving ML model performance in predicting OPV device efficiency.

failure_paths.value: partial: Incorporating device fabrication parameters into ML models Evidence: While including these features did not significantly improve model performance, suggesting limitations in data quality and sparsity.

partial: Using graph neural networks (GNN) for molecular structure encoding Evidence: GNN regressor struggled due to the size of the dataset, but graph embeddings extracted from GNN combined with tree-based models outperformed direct PCE prediction from the graph.
